summary: The executor completed T-L1-mechanism-bridge. It defined P as the surrounding RNA-rich phase, V as the RNA-poor cavity phase, and X as a proposed species; crucially, X would need to form a macroscopic interposed layer for the three-interface spreading coefficient S_X = gamma_PV - gamma_PX - gamma_XV to be the complete-wetting criterion. All gamma and S terms have units of energy/area. Molecular adsorption and boundary enrichment alone do not establish a separate X-rich phase, complete wetting, or a reduction in interfacial free energy. E01-E05 do not identify transcribed X or measure its cavity-boundary enrichment. The search return S-L1-interface-wetting_S1 only supports broad coupled associative/segregative phase-transition context for multivalent proteins and nucleic acids; it gives no internal RNA boundary-wetting result. S2 is not mechanism-relevant; a second targeted search returned no records. I therefore revise the hypothesis to distinguish adsorption from macroscopic complete wetting and keep both untested. The discriminating observation remains calibrated, sequence-specific boundary enrichment relative to adjacent dense phase, but it supports adsorption only and would not alone prove tension reduction or cavity stabilization. I assign a narrow follow-up to verify the generic three-phase criterion and its phase-topology assumptions from eligible background.

hypotheses.statement: A putative minority RNA species X may adsorb preferentially at the internal P-V boundary and alter its interfacial free energy, potentially stabilizing cavities. A stronger and distinct complete-wetting version requires a macroscopic X-rich interposed layer and S_X >= 0. Neither version is established by the supplied data. The adsorption version does not by itself imply a third bulk phase or satisfy the complete-wetting criterion.
assumptions: A non-reference transcript X is produced; DNA read frequency cannot quantify its RNA abundance.
The dark internal region corresponds to a distinct phase boundary P-V rather than an imaging or population artifact.
X has boundary affinity and its adsorption changes interfacial free energy; both are unmeasured.
For the complete-wetting subcase only, an X-rich layer can be treated as a macroscopic intervening phase with well-defined pairwise interfaces.
hypotheses.equation: For the macroscopic-layer subcase only, S_X = gamma_PV - gamma_PX - gamma_XV; S_X >= 0 is the proposed complete-wetting condition under this convention.
